hunks.baseline: In the hazy darkness where he couldn’t see an inch ahead, Jin Mukyung stared—not with his eyes, but with his heart—at the only path laid out before him.
hunks.sol: In the hazy darkness, unable to see an inch ahead, Jin Mukyung faced the only path left to him. He saw it not with his eyes, but with his heart.

hunks.baseline: A future that couldn’t be the future.
hunks.sol: A future that could never come to pass.

hunks.baseline: Even Jin Mukyung was surprised by how calmly he accepted reality in that moment.
hunks.sol: Even Jin Mukyung was surprised by how calmly he accepted it.

hunks.baseline: He’d fought with all his strength, enough to look up at the heavens without a shred of shame. At last, that strength had run out.
hunks.sol: He’d fought with all his strength, hard enough to look up at the heavens without a shred of shame. Now that strength was gone.

hunks.baseline: He’d poured everything into the fight. There was nothing left.
hunks.sol: He’d poured everything into the fight. There was nothing left. In a world that had slowed to a crawl, he watched a spear rise and knew the death in its blade was drawing near, yet he couldn’t twitch a finger.

hunks.baseline: In a world that had slowed to a crawl, he couldn’t even twitch a finger as a spear rose slowly and the death dwelling in its blade drew near.
And yet, if a thread of regret still remained somewhere deep in his heart, it was for those he would leave behind in this world.
hunks.sol: And still, somewhere deep in his heart, one thread of regret remained. It was for the people he would leave behind.

hunks.baseline: He didn’t care what the afterlife was like.
hunks.sol: He didn’t care what awaited him after death.

hunks.baseline: Even if a pale-faced Grim Reaper, dressed head to toe in black, appeared right now, bound him in chains, and dragged him before Yama, it wouldn’t matter.
hunks.sol: Even if a pale-faced Grim Reaper dressed head to toe in black appeared right now, bound him in chains, and dragged him before Yama, it wouldn’t matter.

hunks.baseline: He had lived an honorable life as a martial artist, as the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s Second Young Master.
hunks.sol: He had lived an honorable life as a martial artist and as the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s Second Young Master. The lives he’d taken had been taken to protect others, not because he wanted to kill.

hunks.baseline: The blood on his hands had come from protecting others, not from a desire to kill.
He had to leave everyone behind and be dragged beyond the unknown darkness.
hunks.sol: He had to leave everyone behind and be dragged into the unknown darkness. Not by choice.

hunks.baseline: Not by his own choice, but by someone else’s.
Leaving here everything he had wanted to protect, but in the end had failed to save.
hunks.sol: Everything he’d wanted to protect, everything he had ultimately failed to save, would remain here.

hunks.baseline: In that instant, Jin Mukyung clenched his teeth.
hunks.sol: Jin Mukyung clenched his teeth.

hunks.baseline: He forced his fading consciousness awake and screamed silently in his heart.
hunks.sol: He forced his fading consciousness awake and screamed silently.

hunks.baseline: Everything he could?
hunks.sol: *Everything I could?*

hunks.baseline: What did that even mean?
How could he accept death so weakly?
hunks.sol: What did that even mean? How could he accept death so easily?

hunks.baseline: If he was still alive, then it wasn’t over until his last breath was gone.
hunks.sol: If he was still alive, it wasn’t over. Not until his last breath.

hunks.baseline: He had to get up. He had to fight until the very moment his pounding heart stopped.
hunks.sol: He had to get up. He had to fight until his pounding heart stopped.

hunks.baseline: His fingertips trembled.
The taste of blood filled his mouth between his clenched teeth.
hunks.sol: His fingertips trembled. The metallic taste of blood filled his mouth.

hunks.baseline: But the body he’d tried to rouse, even by biting his own tongue, had long since reached its limit. The cruel reality didn’t change.
hunks.sol: But even biting his own tongue couldn’t rouse a body that had long since passed its limit. The cruel reality didn’t change.

hunks.baseline: The sound of something cutting through the air rang clearly in his ears. In his blurred vision, the slanting flash seemed unusually slow.
hunks.sol: The sound of the spear cutting through the air rang clear in his ears. In his blurred vision, the flash slanting toward him seemed unusually slow.

hunks.baseline: Slow enough for him to look back on his entire life.
hunks.sol: Slow enough to look back on his entire life.

hunks.baseline: Slow enough for him to think of the most irritating person in the world.
hunks.sol: Slow enough to picture the most infuriating face in the world.

hunks.baseline: *If you’d been here in my place… things would’ve been different. Everything.*
hunks.sol: *If you were here instead of me… everything would be different.*

hunks.baseline: As the spearhead fell toward his head, Jin Mukyung sent his words into the void, where they would reach no one.
hunks.sol: As the spearhead fell toward his head, Jin Mukyung spoke in his heart to the only younger brother he had. The words would never reach him.

hunks.baseline: To his only younger brother, who wasn’t here.
Two years ago, the brothers had made a promise with the wall of the training hall between them.
hunks.sol: Two years ago, the brothers had made a promise through the wall of the training hall.

hunks.baseline: They’d meet at the Star-Array Grand Banquet.
hunks.sol: They would meet at the Star-Array Grand Banquet, the gathering of countless stars that lit up the world.

hunks.baseline: At the feast of countless stars that illuminated the world.
In the end, Jin Mukyung had failed to keep that promise.
hunks.sol: In the end, Jin Mukyung hadn’t kept his promise.

hunks.baseline: Because he’d been ashamed. Because he felt his own achievements were nowhere near enough.
hunks.sol: He’d been ashamed. His accomplishments had felt nowhere near enough.

hunks.baseline: When he’d first picked up a sword, he’d wanted to become a great martial artist. After that, he’d wanted to become the pride of the Jin Family of Taiyuan—and a younger brother his elder brother could be proud of.
hunks.sol: When he’d first picked up a sword, he’d wanted to become a great martial artist. Later, he’d wanted to become the pride of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and a younger brother his elder brother could be proud of.

hunks.baseline: But there had been another reason, the greatest one, that he’d spent the past two years swinging his sword without rest in suffocating darkness.
hunks.sol: But there was another reason—his greatest reason—for spending the past two years swinging his sword without rest in suffocating darkness.

hunks.baseline: He’d wanted to become a brother who could hold his head high.
hunks.sol: He wanted to be an older brother who could hold his head high.

hunks.baseline: He wanted to become strong enough to surpass the wall that was Cheongpung, so his younger brother, who’d become the Divine Dragon and soared freely through the sky, wouldn’t be ashamed of him.
hunks.sol: He wanted to grow strong enough to surpass Cheongpung, so his younger brother, soaring through the sky as the Divine Dragon, would have no reason to be ashamed of him.

hunks.baseline: The time of opportunity granted to a young genius, overshadowed by other monsters, was over.
hunks.sol: His time was up: a young genius overshadowed by other monsters.

hunks.baseline: The sword he’d honed in the dark had shone brilliantly enough to light up this gorge today, but that fleeting ray would be swallowed by the long, deep night.
hunks.sol: The sword he’d honed in the dark had shone brightly enough to light this gorge today. But that fleeting light would be swallowed by the long, deep night.

hunks.baseline: Refusing to close his eyes even in the face of death was his pride as a martial artist and proof that his fighting spirit remained unbroken. It was also his chance to say one last goodbye to his troublesome younger brother.
hunks.sol: He would not close his eyes in the face of death. It was the last pride he had as a martial artist, proof that his fighting spirit remained unbroken. And he wanted to say goodbye to his troublesome younger brother, even if his voice would never reach him.

hunks.baseline: Even if his voice would reach no one.
And just as the words were forced through Jin Mukyung’s lips—
hunks.sol: The words had barely left Jin Mukyung’s lips when—

hunks.baseline: Jin Mukyung’s world, dark and hazy until then, turned blue-white. The flash falling toward his head abruptly changed course, whipped aside.
hunks.sol: His world, dark and hazy until then, turned blue-white. The flash falling toward his head changed course and swept sideways.

hunks.baseline: *KWAaaaa!*
hunks.sol: *KRAAAAAASH!*

hunks.baseline: A tremendous shock wave tore across the gorge, its roar deafening.

hunks.baseline: In the distant flash of light that engulfed everything around him, he also made out someone’s hazy back.
hunks.sol: Amid the blinding light that engulfed everything around him, he could just make out someone’s back.

hunks.baseline: *Cough.*
Jin Mukyung spat up dark-red blood and suddenly wondered if he might already be dead.
hunks.sol: Jin Mukyung coughed up dark-red blood. A thought struck him.

hunks.baseline: Perhaps, unable to let go of his attachments from life, he was seeing things even after death.
hunks.sol: Perhaps he was already dead. Perhaps his lingering attachment to life was making him see things even now.

hunks.baseline: It was vivid.
Everything he could see, hear, and feel in that moment was too real to believe it could be granted to the dead.
hunks.sol: Everything he saw, heard, and felt was too vivid to belong to the dead.

hunks.baseline: The stinging pain in his skin where the rock fragments had scraped past. The muscles screaming throughout his body. The blood surging from his insides, twisted by severe Internal Injury.
hunks.sol: The sting where rock fragments had scraped his skin. The muscles screaming throughout his body. The blood rising from his insides, twisted by severe Internal Injury.

hunks.baseline: Jin Mukyung’s body went rigid.
hunks.sol: Jin Mukyung went rigid. His eyes flew wide.

hunks.baseline: His eyes flew wide, a storm raging in their depths.
It was certain.
Not a hallucination. Not a trick of the ears.
hunks.sol: There was no mistaking it. This wasn’t a hallucination. He wasn’t hearing things.

hunks.baseline: “I’d pat you on the back, but, well, the situation’s a little tricky.”
hunks.sol: “I’d give your back a pat, but the timing’s not great.”

hunks.baseline: The voice came through clearly, beyond the roar that was slowly dying away.
hunks.sol: The voice came through clearly as the roar died away.

hunks.baseline: The figure stood out in the fading light.
hunks.sol: In the fading light, he could see him.

hunks.baseline: That irritating voice alone was enough to make his fist clench.
The back of the wastrel, who had somehow grown broader and sturdier than his own.
hunks.sol: That infuriating voice alone was enough to make Jin Mukyung want to raise a fist. That wastrel’s back had, at some point, grown broader and sturdier than his own.

hunks.baseline: Where had that strength come from?
hunks.sol: Where had the strength come from?

hunks.baseline: Jin Mukyung squeezed out a voice rough as scraping metal and raised his hand.
hunks.sol: Jin Mukyung forced the word through a voice rough as scraping metal and raised his hand. His fingertips shook like an aspen leaf as he reached for his only younger brother’s robe.

hunks.baseline: His fingertips trembled like a leaf in a storm, his body already past its limit, as he reached for his only younger brother’s sleeve.
A tiny sound of friction, so faint he had to strain to hear it.
hunks.sol: The sound of fabric brushing against something was so faint he had to strain to hear it.

hunks.baseline: Perhaps it was the wind, not Jin Mukyung’s hand, that brushed the edge of his tattered robe.
hunks.sol: Perhaps it was the wind, not Jin Mukyung’s hand, that touched the edge of the tattered robe.

hunks.baseline: What he wanted to convey wasn’t just a touch. It was his desperate wish for his brother to protect everyone.
hunks.sol: What he wanted to convey was more than a touch. It was a desperate wish for his brother to protect everyone.

hunks.baseline: His hand fell limply. His whole body went slack.
hunks.sol: His hand fell. His whole body went slack.

hunks.baseline: At last, after spending every last bit of his strength, the pathetic older brother lost consciousness.
hunks.sol: At last, the pathetic older brother, having spent every last bit of his strength, lost consciousness.

hunks.baseline: Before him stood his wastrel younger brother, returned from two years away.
hunks.sol: Before him stood his wastrel younger brother, returned after two years away. A dozen *zhang* from him stood an unfamiliar, graying middle-aged man, watching him with a dark, steady gaze.

hunks.baseline: He faced an unfamiliar, graying middle-aged man who stood a dozen *zhang* away, staring straight at him with a somber gaze.
Flames poured from his eyes. His voice, by contrast, was cold as ice.
hunks.sol: His eyes blazed with flame. His voice, by contrast, was cold as ice.

hunks.baseline: “Was it you who beat up my hyung?”
hunks.sol: “Did you beat up my hyung?”

hunks.baseline: As a dragon whose roar shook the heavens.
hunks.sol: A dragon that shook heaven and earth.

hunks.baseline: Beyond his low voice, the people of Shanxi raised tearful cheers that rang out through the gorge.
hunks.sol: Beyond his low voice rose the tearful cheers of the people of Shanxi.

hunks.baseline: A little while ago, someone had told me:
Don’t try to carry everything alone.
hunks.sol: Not long ago, someone told me not to carry everything alone.

hunks.baseline: Try trusting them a little more.
hunks.sol: To trust them a little more.

hunks.baseline: And in that moment, I realized that person had been right.
hunks.sol: Now I knew they’d been right.

hunks.baseline: I could tell as soon as I reached the battlefield.
hunks.sol: I could tell the moment I reached the battlefield.

hunks.baseline: Blood was everywhere. Severed limbs had fallen from bodies I couldn’t identify, and countless corpses of people and horses had piled up into small hills, filling the narrow gorge.
hunks.sol: Blood was everywhere. Limbs torn from bodies I couldn’t identify lay among countless corpses of people and horses. They had piled into small hills that filled the narrow gorge.

hunks.baseline: Most of them were nomads.
hunks.sol: Most of the dead were nomads.

hunks.baseline: The enemy outnumbered us by at least two to one. But even with the odds stacked against them—not just in numbers, but in fighting strength—the people of Shanxi hadn’t given in.
hunks.sol: The enemy had outnumbered the people of Shanxi by at least two to one. They’d been badly outmatched in fighting strength, too. But they hadn’t given in.

hunks.baseline: No. They were squeezing out every last bit of strength to fight back.
hunks.sol: No. They’d fought back with every bit of strength they had.

hunks.baseline: The Imperial Army. The martial artists. Even ordinary people who hadn’t learned so much as a single move of martial arts.
hunks.sol: The Imperial Army. The martial artists. Even ordinary people who probably hadn’t learned a single move of martial arts.

hunks.baseline: And, finally, Jin Mukyung.
hunks.sol: And Jin Mukyung.

hunks.baseline: *They did everything they could. They even overcame their fear of death.*
hunks.sol: *They did everything they could. Even when it meant overcoming their fear of death.*

hunks.baseline: I already knew how hard it was for the weak to stand against the strong.
hunks.sol: I knew how hard it was for the weak to stand against the strong.

hunks.baseline: And I’d taken Jin Mukyung’s wish to heart: there must be no more sacrifices like theirs.
hunks.sol: And I’d taken Jin Mukyung’s wish to heart. There could be no more sacrifices like theirs.

hunks.baseline: White Flame, back from its brief journey, trembled faintly in my grasp.
hunks.sol: White Flame trembled faintly in my grasp, back from its brief journey.
